quests.hint: Regular paid work done for an employer - you can change it if you want something better.
quests.explanation: 'Change her job because she wanted more time for her family' uses a cause-and-effect structure. 'Job' is an essential career word. 'Because' introduces the reason - recognising reason clauses is a key listening comprehension skill.

quests.textWithBlanks: She decided to change her ___ because she wanted more time for her family.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Directions that explain how to do something step by step.
quests.explanation: 'Clear instructions before the project began' is a natural workplace phrase. 'Give instructions' is more formal than 'tell someone what to do.' The adjective 'clear' is a very common collocate - instructions should always be clear.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager gave the team clear instructions before the project began.
quests.textWithBlanks: The manager gave the team clear ___ before the project began.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: To arrive too late to catch a vehicle that has already left.
quests.explanation: 'Missed the bus and had to wait thirty minutes' is a very natural transport inconvenience. 'Miss' here means 'fail to catch' - not 'feel sad about.' The consequence 'had to wait' explains the impact of missing the bus.
quests.textToSpeak: He missed the bus and had to wait for thirty minutes.
quests.textWithBlanks: He ___ the bus and had to wait for thirty minutes.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Rooms or buildings where people do professional work.
quests.explanation: 'Move its offices to a larger building' is a natural business relocation phrase. 'Office' is essential workplace vocabulary. 'Decided to move' suggests a planned, deliberate organizational change.
quests.textToSpeak: The company decided to move its offices to a larger building.
quests.textWithBlanks: The company decided to move its ___ to a larger building.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Reserved a place or appointment in advance - made sure it would be available.
quests.explanation: 'Booked a table at the new Italian restaurant' is a natural dining-out phrase. 'Book' (British English for 'reserve') is the standard verb for making reservations. 'Downtown' means in the central part of the city.
quests.textToSpeak: She booked a table at the new Italian restaurant downtown.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ a table at the new Italian restaurant downtown.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A building where a family lives together.
quests.explanation: 'Helped their parents clean the house on Saturday' is a natural family activity phrase. 'Clean the house' is a common household chore. Saturday is traditionally a cleaning day for many families - a very realistic scenario.
quests.textToSpeak: The children helped their parents clean the house on Saturday.
quests.textWithBlanks: The children helped their parents clean the ___ on Saturday.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A journalist who gathers and writes news stories for the media.
quests.explanation: 'The reporter asked the politician difficult questions' sets up a news or interview scenario. Recognizing professional roles (reporter, politician) is essential for understanding real-world English media content.

quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ asked the politician some difficult questions.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A small folding case for carrying money and cards - easy to lose.
quests.explanation: 'Found a wallet and returned it to the owner' describes an honest action. 'Return' here means 'give back,' not 'go back.' This sentence teaches both vocabulary and the concept of civic responsibility in everyday life.
quests.textToSpeak: She found a wallet on the street and returned it to the owner.
quests.textWithBlanks: She found a ___ on the street and returned it to the owner.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A formal talk delivered to an audience, often with visual aids.
quests.explanation: 'The presentation lasted almost two hours' is a natural professional observation. 'Lasted' means 'continued for' - a common duration verb. 'Almost' softens the statement, showing it was slightly under two hours.
quests.textToSpeak: The presentation lasted almost two hours.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ lasted almost two hours.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A period of time taken off work for travel or rest - very welcome after a busy year.
quests.explanation: 'Saved enough money to go on a holiday abroad' is a natural goal-achievement phrase. 'Go on a holiday' is British English - Americans say 'take a vacation.' 'Abroad' means in another country.
quests.textToSpeak: He saved enough money to go on a holiday abroad.
quests.textWithBlanks: He saved enough money to go on a ___ abroad.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A skilled worker who repairs vehicles and machines.
quests.explanation: 'The mechanic repaired the car in less than an hour' introduces professional vocabulary beyond basic words. 'Mechanic' is specific - different from 'engineer' or 'technician.' 'In less than an hour' is a natural time expression.
quests.textToSpeak: The mechanic repaired the car in less than an hour.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ repaired the car in less than an hour.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Said sorry - expressed regret for something you did wrong.
quests.explanation: 'Apologized for being late to the meeting' is a very natural professional and social expression. 'Apologize for + -ing' is an important grammatical pattern. Notice that 'for' is followed by an -ing form, not a base verb.
quests.textToSpeak: She apologized for being late to the meeting.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ for being late to the meeting.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Feeling sad or let down because something you hoped for did not happen.
quests.explanation: 'Disappointed when the trip was cancelled' expresses emotional letdown. 'Disappointed' is stronger than 'sad' and more specific. The pattern 'was disappointed when' + a negative event is very common in everyday conversation.
quests.textToSpeak: The children were disappointed when the trip was cancelled.
quests.textWithBlanks: The children were ___ when the trip was cancelled.

quests.textWithBlanks: We have to ___ the report by the end of the week.

quests.textToSpeak: He woke up early to watch the sunrise over the mountains.
quests.textWithBlanks: He woke up early to watch the ___ over the mountains.

quests.textToSpeak: She asked her neighbour to water her plants while she was away.
quests.textWithBlanks: She asked her ___ to water her plants while she was away.

quests.textWithBlanks: The doctor said I need to get more ___ and sleep.

quests.textWithBlanks: The meeting was ___ because the manager was ill.

quests.textToSpeak: The airline lost her luggage during the flight to Paris.
quests.textWithBlanks: The airline lost her ___ during the flight to Paris.

quests.textWithBlanks: He takes the ___ train to avoid the traffic.

quests.textWithBlanks: She finished reading the ___ in just three days.

quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ prepared a special menu for the occasion.

quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ was delivered to the wrong address by mistake.

quests.textWithBlanks: She decided to study ___ for one semester.
